messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: latency_p99 breach detected for /v1/generate (model: redwood-large) in eu-west1. p95 ~800ms -> 2.4s, p99 ~11.2s. streaming stalls observed. increased KV cache eviction rate reported. auto-page to oncall.

evan (oncall): saw the page, jumping on it. is paging going to SRE oncall channel also? @mira can you confirm observed metrics?

mira (sre): confirming. dash shows sharp spike starting 15m ago. KV cache evictions/sec went from ~3k -> ~18k. eviction log lines reference prefill jobs + decode misses.

jonas (runtime): logs attached from runtime nodes:

```
[2026-03-15T18:03:10Z] evict: shard=12 used=78% threshold=70% candidate=prefill-req-4932
[2026-03-15T18:03:11Z] warn: decode_cache_miss id=0x7f2c prefill_evicted=true
[2026-03-15T18:03:11Z] stream stall: session=abcd123 delay_ms=4500
```

jonas (runtime): suspicion: prefill tasks are filling KV with prefixes that hurt decode hot-keys -> fragmentation -> tail latency for active requests.

evan (oncall): customers hitting streaming stalls are high-traffic tenants on dedicated capacity. @customer-ops any immediate escalations?

customer-ops: customer A reported repeated stalls ~18:10, error rate up ~12% for them. Customer B (sandbox) also saw degraded streaming. Notified accounts team.

evan (oncall): immediate mitigation plan options:
- throttle/disable prefill globally for eu-west1
- bump KV cache size for affected pools
- enable fallback routing to warm instance pool (lower mem) for critical tenants
- temporarily disable streaming (non-streaming fallback)

mira (sre): agree start with toggling prefill to low rate then disable if not effective. need safe toggle command.

jonas (runtime): runbook toggle:

```
# disable prefill for region
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/regions/eu-west1/overrides \ 
  -d '{"kv_prefill_enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SECRETTOKEN'

# or set rate to 0.1
-d '{"kv_prefill_rate":0.1}'
```

karla (prod-eng): adding: if we disable prefill, we must also shorten prefill TTL to avoid mass eviction waves. otherwise cache will still be full of prefill entries.

evan (oncall): rolling the prefill toggle now. calling it out in ops audit.

evan (oncall): `curl ... overrides` -> 200 OK, kv_prefill_enabled:false returned.

mira (sre): monitoring p95/p99. any immediate change?

jonas (runtime): within 90s, eviction/sec drops from 18k -> 4.2k. decode_miss log rate down too.

mira (sre): p95 improved to ~420ms after 2m, p99 down to ~1.1s after 4m. streaming stalls count decreased by ~85%.

evan (oncall): good delta. customer-ops: any updates from customers?

customer-ops: Customer A reports improvement at 18:18, still seeing a couple stalled streams but vastly better. emailing ops update.

karla (prod-eng): follow-up: we should also patch eviction policy to prefer prefill candidates before decode-hot keys. putting a hot-key bias on eviction will reduce tail latency.

jonas (runtime): agreed. quick mitigation: set eviction_bias = "prefill_first" for eu-west1 pools.

mira (sre): apply config change via runtime flag. note: risk of temporary memory pressure raise on decode path if misconfigured.

jonas (runtime): applying:
```
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/inference runtime_EVICTION_BIAS=prefill_first --record
```

jonas (runtime): change rolled, controllers picked up in ~40s. eviction logs now show prefill entries selected.

mira (sre): monitoring tail. p99 now ~600-800ms and holding. streaming stalls near baseline.

evan (oncall): summarize customer impact: Customer A partial; Customer B recovered; internal alerts still firing for a minority of pods - investigating node-level fragmentation.

karla (prod-eng): notes for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = prefill subsystem started aggressive background fills after a region warmup (spike in traffic + new prefill tuning) which caused KV fragmentation. decode path then faced cold keys and high miss penalty -> streaming stalls.

mira (sre): immediate next steps before we close page:
- keep prefill disabled in eu-west1 for next 6h
- revert recent prefill tuning PR (PR#4523) that changed prefill aggressiveness
- schedule a controlled test of eviction policy with synthetic load
- alert product to pause any new prefill mem-alloc experiments

evan (oncall): I've created a ticket: INF-8342 with mitigation steps and links to graphs/logs.

evan (oncall): handing off to @mira for ownership of postmortem and long-term fix. I'm going offline now.

mira (sre): taking ownership. will coordinate with runtime (jonas) and prod-eng (karla). drafting incident timeline.

jonas (runtime): quick note for the postmortem: capture kernel OOM-kicks? we saw none. it's purely cache fragmentation/eviction churn causing tail latency, not OOM.

karla (prod-eng): also record that temporary routing to fallback model (smaller quantized) was considered but not required.

customer-ops: will send a short incident summary to affected customers and include mitigation timeline.

mira (sre): closing live incident thread now, will post draft postmortem in #incidents in ~3 hours for reviews. leaving prefill disabled and eviction_bias set. if anything regresses, re-open thread or page oncall.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: latency_p99 breach for /v1/generate in eu-west1 mitigated. root cause suspected: KV cache pressure due to aggressive prefill leading to decode-prefill imbalance. Metrics: p99 peak 11.2s -> stable ~0.7s. auto-resolved alerts suppressed for 30m.

mira (sre): final note: mitigation was low-risk toggle + eviction bias change. long term: need better prefill costing, per-tenant prefill quotas, and instrumentation to attribute tail latency to specific eviction candidates.
